items.title: 2026 Winter Olympics open with Alps blanketed in artificial snow

featured_image.name: Italian expert's manufactured snow will play big role at the ...

items.description:
The 2026 Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics, which officially begin on February 6 with a historic dual-location opening ceremony, will depend almost entirely on manufactured snow as warming temperatures and unpredictable natural snowfall reshape the future of winter sports in the Alps.

Organizers have deployed approximately 2.4 million cubic meters of artificial snow across competition venues—equivalent to twice the volume of Rome's Colosseum—requiring roughly 948,000 cubic meters of water and 125 snow cannons to prepare courses for elite athletes.[1][2]

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.6 amid Super Bowl ad clash

featured_image.name: Sam Altman Slams Anthropic Super Bowl Ads Jabbing OpenAI's Ad ...

items.description:
Anthropic and OpenAI are sharpening their competitive edge in a battle for AI supremacy, with both companies unveiling new enterprise products this week while exchanging barbs over dueling Super Bowl advertisements. The public spat between the two startups—whose origins intertwine from OpenAI's own ranks—signals a pivotal moment as both companies race to prove they can build sustainable businesses from their costly AI ventures.

On Wednesday, Anthropic released a series of television ads set to air during Super Bowl LX that mock OpenAI's decision to introduce advertisements into ChatGPT. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responded on X, calling the spots "funny" but "clearly dishonest," accusing Anthropic of "doublespeak." The commercials feature the tagline "Ads coming to AI. But not to Claude" and depict humorous scenarios where an ad-supported chatbot derails user requests with intrusive product placements.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Italy enacts decree allowing police to detain protesters before demonstrations

featured_image.name: Italians Protest US Plans to Deploy ICE at Winter Olympics ...

items.description:
The Italian government on Thursday enacted a sweeping security decree granting police new powers to detain suspected troublemakers for up to 12 hours before public demonstrations, a measure that civil liberties groups condemned as an assault on constitutional rights. The decree came just one day before planned protests at the opening ceremony of the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's cabinet approved the legislation following violent clashes in Turin last weekend, where more than 100 police officers were injured during a demonstration against the closure of the Askatasuna social center, according to the interior ministry. Video footage showed masked protesters attacking an officer with kicks, punches, and hammer blows.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Ukraine and Russia swap 314 prisoners in first exchange in months

featured_image.name: Ukraine and Russia carry out first prisoner exchange in months as U.S. touts "tangible results" in peace talks

items.description:
Ukraine and Russia conducted their first prisoner exchange in five months on Thursday, swapping 157 captives each following two days of US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi that ended without resolving the war's core disputes over territory and ceasefire terms.

The swap brought home 150 Ukrainian military personnel and seven civilians, with most having been held since 2022, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War. Among those freed were 19 Ukrainians who had been illegally sentenced by Russian courts, including 15 serving life imprisonment, Ukrainian intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov confirmed. The youngest released prisoner is 23 years old, having been captured at age 19 during the defense of Mariupol.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: British scientists unveil AI that tracks icebergs from birth to breakup

featured_image.name: Antarctic iceberg the size of Chicago breaks off, reveals ...

items.description:
Scientists at the British Antarctic Survey have unveiled an artificial intelligence system capable of tracking icebergs throughout their entire lifecycle, from the moment they break off from glaciers to their eventual disintegration in open waters, the organization announced Thursday.

The AI tool addresses what researchers have described as a "major blind spot" in climate science by creating detailed "family trees" that link fragmented iceberg pieces back to their original parent formations, something that has not previously been possible at scale.

items.title: Ginkgo Bioworks, OpenAI cut protein costs 40% with GPT-5 lab

featured_image.name: How Ginkgo Bioworks leverages synthetic biology to shape ...

items.description:
Ginkgo Bioworks and OpenAI announced today that their collaboration using a GPT-5-powered autonomous laboratory achieved a 40 percent reduction in cell-free protein synthesis costs, marking a milestone in the application of artificial intelligence to biological research. The biotechnology company reported the system reduced the cost of producing superfolder green fluorescent protein from $698 per gram to $422 per gram over six months of testing.[1][2][3]

The announcement, detailed in a scientific preprint not yet peer-reviewed, describes how the autonomous lab executed more than 36,000 experiments across six iterative cycles and generated nearly 150,000 data points with minimal human involvement. Human roles were primarily limited to reagent preparation, loading and unloading materials, and system oversight, while the AI managed experimental design, execution, data interpretation, and hypothesis generation.[2][4][5][3]

items.title: Study links COVID lockdowns to record methane surge

featured_image.name: COVID-19 Shutdowns Lead to Cleaner Air | AQMD Seeks to ...

items.description:
The pandemic measures that cleared city streets and grounded airplanes created an unexpected consequence: they weakened the atmosphere's ability to scrub away methane, helping to trigger the largest recorded surge in the potent greenhouse gas, according to a new study published in the journal Science.

A team of 41 scientists led by researchers at Peking University found that reductions in hydroxyl radicals during the COVID-19 period from 2020 to 2021, followed by a recovery through 2023, accounted for roughly 80 percent of the interannual variations in methane's growth rate.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump backs UK Chagos deal after reversing earlier criticism

featured_image.name: UK, US agree Chagos air base is of strategic importance after Trump criticism of deal

items.description:
President Donald Trump signaled support on Thursday for Britain's controversial agreement to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, reversing his previous sharp criticism of the deal while warning he retains the right to "militarily secure" the strategically vital Diego Garcia airbase.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he understood the agreement negotiated by Prime Minister Keir Starmer was "the best he could make," according to Reuters. The statement marks a dramatic turnaround from his January remarks when he labeled the same deal "an act of great stupidity" and "total weakness".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump endorses Japan's Takaichi ahead of Sunday election

featured_image.name: Japan's snap elections: A reckless risk or calculated gamble?

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump threw his support behind Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday, days before Japan's snap legislative election, and confirmed that the Japanese leader will visit the White House on March 19.

In a message posted on Truth Social, Trump called Takaichi "a strong, powerful, and wise Leader" who "truly loves her Country," giving what he described as his "Complete and Total Endorsement" of her and her governing coalition ahead of Sunday's vote.[1][2]

"Prime Minister Takaichi is someone who deserves powerful recognition for the job she and her Coalition are doing," Trump wrote, concluding with the all-caps rallying cry: "SHE WILL NOT LET THE PEOPLE OF JAPAN DOWN! Good luck on your very important Sunday Vote".[3]
